findings.title: No independent claim covers cleaning by deflection of the seat without a secondary flow path
findings.attack: Design-around resistance 3. Every independent claim requires a purge gap that is a secondary flow path. [0064] and [0126] state that a flow path enlarged by deflection of the seat remains the main passage, and [0287] reports clean sealing surfaces with cured sealant film on the purge gap surface. A seat that deflects and recovers without a purge gap is outside every claim.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent claim to the snap-back wipe with no purge gap recited. Basis for the two-piece seat at [0182], [0294], [0347]; the one-piece seat ring needs a statement from the inventors.

findings.title: Axially deflecting and tilting elements are described but lie outside every claim
findings.attack: Design-around resistance 3. [0179] describes a disc spring whose rim lifts from a face and states that its deflection is not a radial expansion. The form is disclosed, unclaimed and expressly distinguished from the claims.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Claim a deflectable element and a deflection, with radial expansion in a dependent claim. Basis [0179], [0180].

findings.title: Contact from lift-off avoids "spaced from" and the normal stroke
findings.attack: Design-around resistance 3, evidentiary ease 4. The two ranges of travel are defined by first contact alone. A surface in light contact from the closed position leaves no normal stroke and no over-travel as defined, and the claimant must prove an absence of contact.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a formulation that defines the ranges by the state of the purge gap and by the load. The inventors must confirm that contact below the opening load is within their conception.

findings.title: Claim 2 is performed by the rider and reaches a supplier only indirectly
findings.attack: Infringement detectability 2. Every step is a private act of a user, whether the over-travel is reached depends on the pump, and a supplier is liable only indirectly.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Keep claim 2 and rely on the product claims. [0265] supports a claim to the manufacturer's test of each valve core.

findings.title: Claim 3 is avoided by a part that has no sealing edge or no load-converting geometry of its own
findings.attack: Design-around resistance 3. The wiper ring has no sealing edge and a plain ring spread by a conical surface has no load-converting geometry of its own, so neither part is reached by claim 3.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent claim to a radially deflectable element as a part. Basis [0099], [0164], [0165].

findings.title: The shape-setting step of claim 4 cannot be seen in the product and is avoided by another forming route
findings.attack: Infringement detectability 2, design-around resistance 2. The step leaves no distinguishing mark in the ring and is avoided by cutting the geometry into tube that is already superelastic.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a method claim in which the geometry is formed by laser cutting a pattern in the wall. Treat the manufacturing claims as fallback positions.

assumptions.text: The commercially successful architecture is the form built and tested for Example 1; the package contains no sales or market information.
Novelty and inventive-step resilience are scored against the saved references only; the index states that the search was thin.
Claim 4 is treated as an independent claim concept although it is written by reference to claim 3.
The scores are ordinal judgements; a difference of one point carries no weight.

open_questions.text: Is the product to be sold the one-piece seat ring of superelastic NiTi alloy, or a cheaper form?
Is the replacement-part market for the seat ring large enough to justify the additional independent claim proposed in F-35-5?
For counsel: should claims 2 and 4 be kept as independent claims, given their scores and the claim fees?
